n: Job answers Bildad with biting irony before giving his own hymn to God’s power.
Sarcastically Job asks: what a help you have been to someone so weak! How you have rescued a powerless arm!

f.g: Job himself — Bildad’s words did nothing to help.

n: What wonderful advice you’ve given to someone without wisdom! What deep insight you have shared!
Job asks who helped Bildad say these things — whose spirit was speaking through him? He implies the words were borrowed and empty.
Job now describes God’s power even over the realm of the dead. The departed spirits beneath the waters tremble before him.

f.g: Hebrew rephaim — the shades or spirits of the dead.

n: The place of the dead is laid bare before God; nothing is hidden from him, not even destruction itself.

f.g: Hebrew sheol — the world of departed spirits, not necessarily a place of punishment.
Hebrew Abaddon, a poetic name for the realm of the dead.

n: God stretches out the northern sky over empty space and hangs the earth on nothing — a striking image of God’s sustaining power.
God wraps up water in clouds like skins of water, yet the clouds don’t burst under the weight.

f.w: bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds

n: He covers the face of his throne, spreading clouds over it. God’s glory is veiled from human sight.
He draws a circle on the surface of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness — the horizon.
The pillars holding up the sky shake and are stunned at God’s rebuke.

f.g: Poetic image of mountains that seem to hold up the sky.

n: By his power God calms (or stirs) the sea, and by his skill he strikes down Rahab, the proud sea monster.

f.g: Hebrew Rahab — a poetic name for a chaos monster of the sea, symbolizing forces opposed to God.

n: By his breath the skies became clear, and his hand pierced the fleeing serpent. God has defeated every power of chaos.

f.g: The “gliding serpent,” a symbol of chaos and evil.

n: All these wonders are just the edges of God’s ways — a mere whisper. Who could ever understand the full thunder of his power?

f.w: how little a portion is heard of him?
